summary.title: Collision detection
summary.one_liner: Learn how to detect collisions between axis-aligned bounding boxes and between a circle and a box, as used in a Breakout-style 2D game in OpenGL.
takeaways: Simple shapes such as AABBs and circles are used as approximations for collision tests instead of complex object geometry.
Two AABBs collide when their edges overlap on both the x and y axes.
A circle-AABB collision is found by clamping the difference vector between centers to the box extents to get the closest point, then comparing the distance to the radius.
Collision handling in the game loop checks each non-destroyed brick against the ball and destroys non-solid bricks on contact.
The page notes that bounding shapes can report collisions that do not occur with the real shape, and that ball response is covered in the next chapter.
summary.summary: The tutorial explains why simple shapes are used for collision detection instead of an object's real vertex data, and notes their approximation drawbacks. It first implements AABB-AABB overlap testing in C++ with glm-style vectors, then wires it into a DoCollisions function that destroys non-solid bricks. It then shows why a rectangle is a poor fit for the round ball and implements a more precise circle-versus-AABB test by clamping the center difference vector to the box half-extents. The page ends by noting that the ball does not yet respond to collisions, which is deferred to the next chapter.
